source: Energy Aspects — crude arbs (Argus Media Group, LSEG, CME, Energy Aspects)

note.headline: Dubai recovered from a weak start to January trade as Asian margins strengthened. Arbs to Asia softened w/w, but the Atlantic has to keep discounting to fill Asia's Q1-27 gap.
note.verdict: East of Suez is the tight market. The Atlantic has to clear cheaply into it: WAF and LatAm are open into Asia, while US barrels (WTI, Mars) are marginal or closed and Middle East sours are shut out of the West.
ea: Hormuz: STS constraints persist. Middle East Gulf flows can be sustained at around 11 mb/d through STS, with weekly loadings picking up to more than 6 vessels a day. Asia is increasingly exposed to supply disruptions.

Atlantic to Asia: WTI became marginal into Asia late last week, but LatAm and WAF grades will dominate Atlantic flows. European and US forward balances remain oversupplied, so softer diffs are needed to pull crude East. Atlantic fixtures to Asia need to pick up m/m for Dec-loading to ease Asian tightness in Q1-27.

Sweet, Americas: LatAm dominates, and Brazil absorbs most incoming VLCC tonnage. Weaker Tupi diffs put it in Asian optimised slates, replacing Castilla. Nov-loading USGC fixtures to Asia are below their 11-month minimum and LatAm fixtures above their maximum. WTI arbs to Asia weakened w/w to marginal as Murban fell at the start of Dubai trading.

Sweet, WAF: flows favour Asia, whose forward balances are tighter than Europe's, and Atlantic inflows to Asia fall sharply from January. Europe's optimised slate favours residue-rich LatAm and WAF (Girassol leads the mediums). Lights are priced out except CPC. WAF to Europe is marginal on paper but closes once Ekofisk is reassessed lower.

Sour: North American sour oversupply keeps US sour diffs weak, and Oman needs to be stronger to open arbs to Asia. SPR releases from Texas caverns are hitting SGC (about $9/bbl discounts) harder than Mars. Mars is closed to Europe and Asia: it weakened w/w to Asia on softer Oman and improved to Europe on lower TD25.
ours: Azeri (SOCAR): NWE is the only open outlet, at +1.02 to +2.05 $/bbl and widening to Mar-27. It is closed to Asia-Pac (−5.57 Feb, −4.92 Mar) and the USGC (−24 to −30).
CPC is open everywhere it's quoted: Med +24 to +25, NWE +12 to +13, Asia-Pac +6 to +7. It is the main competitor for light sweet slots in the Med and NWE.
North Sea lights are shut into the Med: Ekofisk −15 to −18, Forties −10 to −13. Forties into Asia is −7.49 Feb, narrowing to −5.17 Mar.
WAF: Cabinda (+12.5–12.8) and Forcados (+9.3–9.5) are wide open into Asia-Pac. Into India only Dalia is open (+2.6 to +6.1); Agbami, Bonny and Forcados are −3 to −9, narrowing into Mar.
Middle East sour is shut West: Basrah and Arab Light are −17 to −33 into NWE, the Med and the USGC, but Arab Lt (+8.6/+8.9) and Basrah Hvy (+2.5/+2.7) are open into India.
Heavy Canadian/LatAm open: WCS is open in every table (+2.3 to +14.5). Castilla is wide open to Asia-Pac (+11–12) but closed to India (−4.7 to −1.5).
note.trade: Place Azeri into NWE rather than offering it East. Expect CPC to keep pressing Med light sweet diffs, and stay positioned for CPC to stay cheap against Azeri/BTC while CPC's arbs are this wide open.
note.kill: Oman/Dubai firming enough to push WTI into Asia above about +2 (more US competition East), or the Azeri NWE arb turning negative.
note.caveat: Typed in by hand from EA's crude arbs report (3 Nov 2026; sources: Argus, LSEG, CME, EA). Positive = arb open (the grade is economic in that destination), negative = closed. Blanks are months EA doesn't assess. The w/w sparklines in EA's tables aren't transcribed; the w/w comments come from EA's text.
